transcript:
Header: 2026-09-15 16:00 UTC - Duration: 54m
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Sara Park (Head of Search, LexiSearch), Tom Nguyen (ML Engineer), Priya Menon (CTO)

00:00 - 00:22 Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, excited to walk through how our hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints can slot into LexiSearch's stack. Quick intro from our side, i'm aisha, i'm the AE; miguel is our solutions engineer.
00:23 - 00:40 Sara: hey hi thanks, sara here. we run search for a docs+kb product, main pain is relevance at top results and reducing manual curation.
00:41 - 01:05 Miguel: cool; quick agenda - show embeddings pipeline, similarity search patterns, then rerank endpoint and how you can combine both for lightweight rerank without shipping whole model. we'll demo console + API snippets, then discuss perf/cost and security.
01:06 - 01:40 Priya: timeline wise we want a small pilot in the next 2 weeks; success is measurable lift in MRR search relevance metric and sub-200ms p99 on host calls ideally.
01:41 - 02:10 Aisha: noted - we'll capture that as success criteria. quick q - are you currently using vector db or self-hosted FAISS?
02:11 - 03:02 Tom: we use a hosted vector DB (vendor name redacted), but it's getting costly at scale and we lose some control over rerank prompts. We're exploring alternatives: move to hybrid approach (ANN + small rerank model).
03:03 - 04:00 Miguel: that's a familiar pattern. the Redwood hosted API supports embeddings generation + a dedicated rerank endpoint: get top-K via your ANN, then call rerank with the candidate docs + query to reorder with model signals. avoids needing to run a full cross-encoder at index time.
04:01 - 04:30 Sara: ok can you show the console flow? how do we visualize embeddings quality and do quick A/B?
04:31 - 06:00 Miguel: demo on screen - Console > Models > Embeddings. you can run a batch embed, see token counts, latency distributions, and token cost estimates. show sample run: 5 queries -> embed -> cosine similarity -> rerank call using rerank endpoint. note: the rerank endpoint accepts up to N candidates (we demo with 10) and returns score + structured output. (transcription muffled)
06:01 - 06:40 Tom: how do you handle out-of-vocab or company-specific names? our docs have many product codes and acronyms.
06:41 - 07:20 Miguel: embeddings are robust; we recommend custom tokenization if extreme, but more commonly customers add alias lists or use a lightweight preprocessor. also we support passing metadata through for rerank so you can bias by recency or doc type.
07:21 - 08:05 Priya: security - we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, and KMS-managed keys; data residency US-EU only.
08:06 - 09:00 Aisha: yes we are SOC2, have SSO/SAML, provide customer-managed KMS support for private deployments. for hosted API we offer options: encryption at rest, separation by tenant, and audit logs. we'll share the security pack after the call.
09:01 - 10:00 Miguel: back to rerank: architecture slide - you usually run an ANN (we support integrations with Pinecone, Weaviate, or self-hosted Faiss) to get top-k. then either 1) light rerank API call to use our tuned transformer for pairwise scoring, or 2) host a heavier cross-encoder if you want offline indexing. the rerank endpoint is optimized for low-latency: we do continuous batching under the hood to preserve SLOs.
10:01 - 11:20 Sara: what's the per-call latency and cost tradeoff? we care about p99 under 200ms for the rerank call if possible.
11:21 - 12:30 Miguel: typical p50 is ~40-60ms for 10 candidates on hosted, p95 around 120ms, p99 depends on payload size. cost depends on token count and model. we can tune with fewer candidates, caching of prefixes, or using cheaper model variants for rerank. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and model variant that reduce unit cost.
12:31 - 14:00 Tom: can you show an API example? we want to see request/response shapes.
14:01 - 16:30 Miguel: sure - quick code snippet: POST /v1/embeddings with documents array -> returns vectors; then POST /v1/rerank with {query, candidates: [{id, text, metadata}], top_k: 5} -> returns scores + normalized ranking. (Miguel pastes curl and node SDK). Also showed pseudo-output: [{id: 'doc3', score:0.92}, ...].
16:31 - 17:10 Sara: do you support streaming for rerank or just sync?
17:11 - 17:55 Miguel: rerank is synchronous (since it needs the full candidate list) but is low-latency; generation endpoints support streaming.
17:56 - 19:00 Priya: on the samples you showed, how do we evaluate relevance lift? we need A/B framework suggestions.
19:01 - 20:10 Miguel: we recommend canary traffic split in console - route small % to rerank-enabled pipeline, measure top-k click-through and MRR. console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and you can set alerts on quality regressions tied to prompt sets.
20:11 - 21:30 Tom: our index size is ~3m docs, but candidate set for any query is usually capped at 200. any special indexing recommendations?
21:31 - 22:50 Miguel: for 3m docs, use ANN to filter to 100-200 candidates; then rerank top 10. if your queries are short, you can aggressively prune and cache embeddings for popular prefixes using Redwood's KV cache. Also quantization recommendations and model selection from Redwood Optimize will help.
22:51 - 24:00 Sara: do you have any benchmarks vs running a cross-encoder locally? we have a small infra team considering hosting a cross-encoder on dedicated GPUs.
24:01 - 25:30 Miguel: cross-encoders at index time yield best quality but cost is higher. we did benchmarks: our rerank endpoint delivered ~95% of cross-encoder lift for many ecom/docs workloads at ~25-40% of the cost and lower infra overhead. we can share benchmark spreadsheet.
25:31 - 27:00 Priya: data privacy question - can we restrict logs and ensure no PII is persisted?
27:01 - 28:20 Aisha: yes hosted offerings include configurable retention, option to disable logging for specific endpoints, and contract terms for data handling. for stricter needs, dedicated or private deployment with customer-managed KMS is recommended.
28:21 - 29:40 Tom: what's the integration effort? coms say a week?
29:41 - 31:00 Miguel: pilot with 5k queries: we provide SDK snippets, a bench script to run embeddings+ANN+rerank, and a sample dashboard. if you have engineers for 1-2 days, we can get bootstrap results quickly. full production depends on your infra and auth flows.
31:01 - 32:20 Sara: curious about rerank prompt control - can we inject business rules to bump certain types of docs?
32:21 - 33:10 Miguel: yes you can pass metadata and bias rules; rerank supports structured signals and you can weight model score + business score. we demoed a simple recency bias in the console.
33:11 - 35:00 Priya: any limits on candidate payload size? some docs are long.
35:01 - 36:20 Miguel: we recommend passing excerpts for rerank; the endpoint has a payload size limit per request but you can include metadata or summarized text. we also support on-the-fly truncation and token estimates in SDKs.
36:21 - 38:00 Tom: how about cost control - if we run large traffic, how to avoid runaway token costs?
38:01 - 39:20 Aisha: Redwood Optimize will surface suggestions - batching, quantization, cheaper model variants - and you can set token quotas and per-route budgets in the console. plus rate limiting and alerts.
39:21 - 41:00 Sara: ok show me the rerank response again, and how to interpret confidence scores.
41:01 - 42:30 Miguel: shows response: score is normalized probability-like; we advise using relative scores for tie-breaking and combining with business weights. console visualizes score distributions and historical drift.
42:31 - 44:00 Tom: any prebuilt connectors for Pinecone/Weaviate?
44:01 - 45:20 Miguel: yes we have integrations and examples in our SDK; you can also bring your ANN - we provide sync scripts for bulk embedding ingestion.
45:21 - 46:30 Priya: cost estimate for pilot?
46:31 - 48:00 Aisha: we'll send a TCO comparing hosted vs dedicated. for a 2-week pilot at your scale (5k queries), hosted token + rerank costs are minimal; dedicated is only recommend if you need sustained high throughput or strict data residency.
48:01 - 50:00 Sara: internal stakeholders - ops and legal will want security docs. please include SOC2 and SSO detail and a sample SLA.
50:01 - 51:20 Aisha: yes will send security pack and sample SLA; we can also set up a dedicated private deployment briefing if needed.
51:21 - 53:00 Miguel: last bit - quick checklist for pilot: provide sample queries + doc corpus, we supply bench script and rerank templates, run A/B, iterate on candidate K and prompt.
53:01 - 54:00 Aisha: recap - Aisha to send pricing + security docs, Miguel to send rerank templates and bench script, Tom to share sample queries; schedule pilot kickoff next week. thanks all.

Notes: small amount of transcription artifact - names occasionally mis-typed (e.g., pinecone pronounced as pine-cone), a few timestamps overlap during screen-share. Recorded on Redwood AE's calendar.
